acceptance: Discovery mode shows three panes: Sources (a box each for YouTube, Spotify, and ffmpeg format) | Inbox (flat table in arrival order) | Inspector.
Inbox rows: select checkbox, title, artist, source, status, match confidence.
Pasting a video title together with its link works; bracketed noise like [Official Music Video] is stripped and the title split into artist and title.

Inspector: every tag field says where its value came from (video title, channel, YouTube release date, upload date, lookup, chosen release) and offers alternatives from other sources; a missing or doubtful field is visibly flagged.
Also in the Inspector: the video's own title, an already-in-library warning, and the destination path (Artist/Album/NN Title.ext).
Year: YouTube's release_date first, else upload_date; when it is only the upload date, say so and ask for a check.

Auto-add is OPT-IN (off by default). When on, a song is added automatically only if its match is at or above the user's threshold (default 70%), every key tag is filled in, and it is not already in the library. Everything auto-added is listed with an Undo.

Auto-add supersedes the earlier rule 'never write tags without an explicit confirm' only for imported songs and only while the user has switched it on; manual Add stays available, and anything below the threshold waits for review.
Spotify links show which tracks are owned and which are missing, and can fetch the missing ones (needs a developer client ID for the login).
Tags are pulled in from real sources where possible: what the link provides, embedded tags in the fetched file, then MusicBrainz lookups; anything guessed is flagged for review.

findings.youtube_metadata_for_example: yt-dlp returns title, channel/uploader, release_date, duration and a thumbnail; no album or track number (those only exist on auto-generated Topic uploads). Album needs a MusicBrainz lookup.
findings.undo_and_staging: Undo of an auto-add is only safe if the file can be moved back out of the library, which is why the staging-folder decision matters.
